aria_snapshot:
- main:
  - paragraph: Research snapshot · 15 Sep 2026
  - heading "Use the panda as a scout, not the whole army." [level=1]
  - paragraph: Lightpanda can take high-volume, public, read-only work off the expensive Chromium queue. It should not inherit logged-in sessions, social actions, checkout, CAPTCHA handling, or visual verification.
  - complementary "Recommendation":
    - text: Recommendation
    - heading "Pilot one sweep behind an automatic fallback." [level=2]
    - paragraph: Keep Chromium as the authority for high-fidelity and authenticated work. Measure how much public research Lightpanda can reliably absorb.
  - text: Status
  - strong: Beta
  - text: Project says errors and crashes remain possible. Interface
  - strong: CDP
  - text: Existing Puppeteer/Playwright code can target its WebSocket endpoint. Vendor claim
  - strong: 9× / 16×
  - text: Faster / less memory on the project's 100-page benchmark. License
  - strong: AGPL-3.0
  - text: Network use and modifications deserve legal review. 01 / routing
  - heading "Choose the cheapest browser that can tell the truth." [level=2]
  - paragraph: Click a workload to see the recommended execution tier. The rule is fidelity first, then cost.
  - group "Workload selector":
    - button "Public research sweep 01" [pressed]
    - button "Bulk link discovery 02"
    - button "Logged-in social action 03"
    - button "Visual QA / screenshot 04"
    - button "Bot-protected target 05"
  - text: Best fit
  - heading "Lightpanda first, Chromium fallback" [level=3]
  - paragraph: Public pages, many URLs, no login, and text extraction are Lightpanda's strongest fit. Escalate on missing content, runtime errors, or challenge pages.
  - text: Tier 0
  - strong: HTTP parser
  - text: No JavaScript route here Tier 1
  - strong: Lightpanda
  - text: JS-lite, text-first Tier 2
  - strong: Chromium
  - text: Full fidelity + sessions Tier 3
  - strong: Managed hard-target browser
  - text: Anti-bot / observability
  - code: public + read_only + text_output → lightpanda → fallback_on(error | missing_content | challenge)
  - text: 02 / landscape
  - heading "Lightpanda is a middle tier, not a universal replacement." [level=2]
  - paragraph: The strongest stack combines zero-browser crawling, a lightweight JS tier, full Chromium, and a managed option only for genuinely hard targets.
  - article:
    - text: JS-lite browser
    - heading "Lightpanda" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Purpose-built in Zig for machine-driven browsing, with V8 and partial Web APIs but no layout engine.
    - term: Best at
    - definition: Public text extraction at high concurrency
    - term: Tradeoff
    - definition: Beta stability and partial site compatibility
    - term: Source
    - definition:
      - link "Official repository ↗":
        - /url: https://github.com/lightpanda-io/browser
  - article:
    - text: No-browser crawler
    - heading "Crawlee" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Mature crawl orchestration with HTTP/DOM parsers, queues, retries, autoscaling, and browser escalation.
    - term: Best at
    - definition: Discovery, queues, datasets, polite crawling
    - term: Tradeoff
    - definition: Cheerio mode cannot execute JavaScript
    - term: Source
    - definition:
      - link "Project mirror ↗":
        - /url: https://github.com/api-evangelist/crawlee
  - article:
    - text: Full-fidelity local
    - heading "Chrome Headless Shell" [level=3]
    - paragraph: A slimmer official Chromium binary for automation that retains web-platform fidelity and real rendering.
    - term: Best at
    - definition: Visual output and complex sites
    - term: Tradeoff
    - definition: Still carries Chromium's resource cost
    - term: Source
    - definition:
      - link "Puppeteer reference ↗":
        - /url: https://github.com/koenhagen/puppeteer
  - article:
    - text: Self-hosted agent API
    - heading "Steel.dev" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Apache-licensed, agent-native browser service with session persistence and CAPTCHA tooling.
    - term: Best at
    - definition: Persistent agent sessions under your control
    - term: Tradeoff
    - definition: Still Chromium underneath
    - term: Source
    - definition:
      - link "Comparison source ↗":
        - /url: https://medium.com/@alexanie/which-cloud-browser-to-choose-testmu-ai-vs-steel-dev-5c00ac12aadb
  - article:
    - text: Managed Chrome fleet
    - heading "Browserless" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Connect over CDP to managed or self-hosted Chromium with production fleet operations handled for you.
    - term: Best at
    - definition: Production Chrome without owning orchestration
    - term: Tradeoff
    - definition: Per-session cost and Chromium footprint
    - term: Source
    - definition:
      - link "Roundup source ↗":
        - /url: https://medium.com/@kevinmenesesgonzalez/best-5-browser-automation-api-for-ai-agents-in-2026-38d179210293
  - article:
    - text: Extraction API
    - heading "Firecrawl" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Single API that returns structured Markdown/JSON and can add a browser when JavaScript is needed.
    - term: Best at
    - definition: Low-integration content extraction
    - term: Tradeoff
    - definition: Less browser control; API cost at scale
    - term: Source
    - definition:
      - link "Comparison source ↗":
        - /url: https://dev.to/apify/firecrawl-vs-apify-2025-guide-for-ai-and-data-teams-42e3
  - text: 03 / reality check
  - heading "The savings are plausible. The edge cases are where trust leaks." [level=2]
  - paragraph: Vendor benchmarks are directional. The pilot should measure content fidelity and fallback rate before it measures speed.
  - text: What it supports
  - heading "Enough browser to execute, not enough browser to render." [level=3]
  - paragraph: Lightpanda exposes CDP and WebDriver BiDi, runs V8, parses HTML, supports DOM APIs, XHR/Fetch, cookies, click and form input, headers, proxies, and network interception.
  - list:
    - listitem: One-shot Markdown/HTML dumps are ideal for agent ingestion.
    - listitem: A CDP endpoint means existing automation can often swap targets.
    - listitem:
      - code: "--obey-robots"
      - text: and per-domain throttles fit research sweeps.
  - strong: Partial APIs
  - text: Modern SPAs, service workers, IndexedDB, canvas, and WebGL can fail or misbehave.
  - strong: No stealth
  - text: Challenge pages and bot protections are escalation signals, not something to work around.
  - strong: Session risk
  - text: Keep authenticated social and identity-sensitive work in the existing Chromium profile.
  - strong: Telemetry
  - text: It is on by default. Disable it for internal operations with the documented environment flag.
  - strong: License
  - text: AGPL-3.0 needs a one-time legal check, especially before serving a modified build over a network. 04 / pilot
  - heading "Start with one boring sweep and make the routing prove itself." [level=2]
  - paragraph: The best first test is a scheduled public-page monitor that already creates pressure on the leased Chromium queue.
  - text: Two-week pilot
  - heading "Public review and business-page monitoring" [level=3]
  - list:
    - listitem:
      - text: Pin a tested Lightpanda build. Do not float on
      - code: nightly
      - text: .
    - listitem: Fetch in Lightpanda first, storing URL, timestamp, status, tool version, and content digest.
    - listitem: Escalate failures, missing-content checks, or challenge signals to Chromium.
    - listitem: Spot-check extracted facts against Chromium before expanding scope.
  - text: Primary gate
  - strong: Fallback rate
  - text: "Target suggested by the report: under roughly 20% before expanding. Truth gate"
  - strong: Content fidelity
  - text: Compare critical fields against Chromium samples. Leverage
  - strong: Queue relief
  - text: How many tasks no longer wait on the leased browser? Efficiency
  - strong: Pages / CPU / RAM
  - text: Measure on the real workload, not vendor benchmarks. ✓ Bind CDP to loopback or an internal network only. ✓ Disable telemetry and suppress core dumps on shared hosts. ✓ Never copy cookies from the leased profile into the pool. ✓ Honor robots directives, Retry-After, site terms, and domain limits. 05 / sources
